newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast Treasury takes over debt management.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast Treasury takes over debt management.

text.p: The management of Ivory Coast's public debt is being transfered to the Treasury from the state bank that has run it until now, the Caisse autonome d'amortissement (CAA), the government said in a statement.
The Treasury will also take over the management of operations co-funded by aid donors, it added.

The CAA will continue to handle the deposits of state firms and various state funds, and will also now manage money from savings banks, pension funds and the Caisse de Stabilisation (Caistab), the state commodity marketing body.
Donors want the Caistab to withdraw from commodity marketing as part of liberalisation terms linked to a $150 million loan dating to 1995.

The government said the aim of the CAA move was to focus the bank's activities more clearly on development work, entailing an extension of its banking side to satisfy the economy's need for investment.
To supplement the funds it collects, the CAA will also be able to issue bonds and other types of negotiable paper, either for its own account or for third parties.
The government said the CAA would work with both the private and public sectors.
The statement said the CAA, which was founded the year before independence from France in 1959, had a capital base of five billion CFA francs ($8 million).
At the end of 1996, it had customer deposits of 203 billion CFA francs and outstanding loans of 170.3 billion.
"Out of this total, the importance of medium- and long-term credits to customers confirms the development bank role that the CAA plays," the government said.
It said the CAA change was part of a general programme of public finance reforms, including the move to a unified state budget.
